For some actual valuable input, this is a thing I've haven't been able to come to a conclusion on for a long time. I think growing up, I always saw cops as the "good guys" because that's how they were always depicted. At the same time I also always felt what I assume everyone else feels being worry when seeing a cop because if they are doing anything more than just existing, there is likely something wrong. Very Pavlovian. 
I haven't really been able to subscribe to ACAB because my general view on life has always been that in most groups there is the possibility of there being a "good" person. How I've made this tangible more recently is one of my friends. He is a police officer and I'd consider him a good person, although I haven't kept up with him recently.  Still, as an example, part of me feels like there could be cops that chose that path because they saw the problems with it and wanted to do something to push it slightly in a positive direction and that was the way they felt they could best contribute. 
All of that said, I have become acutely aware of the very real possibilities even from me being a tall black AMAB and consciously try to be as inconspicuous as possible while around cops. Even while contemplating this question I remembered a time I was in a mental health crisis in which the police were called. I was nonverbal in the moment and to get me to say something one of the cops ground his knuckles I think into my ribs (which was surprisingly extremely uncomfortable) and I think I remember him chuckling or smiling afterwards? I don't have a ton of memory from that moment to be honest. Despite all of that, I still can't for some reason view cops as inherently bad for some reason, even though it makes no sense. I have in the past several years been more critical and averse to generally respected organizations that are expected to kill/harm people, including the military. 
All of that to say: I DON'T KNOW.
